key_risks: Rapid de-escalation or free transit restoration in the Strait of Hormuz could reverse the oil premium before July 20
USO futures roll and high volatility can produce large drawdowns even if spot crude stays elevated
June CPI or Fed-related testimony could reprice rates and risk assets, pressuring financials and equity energy names
Bank earnings misses on July 14 would undercut the FINANCIALS allocation

portfolio.rationale: Hormuz control claims, US blockade restart July 14, and Brent already +9.6% create near-term supply-risk premium that can lift crude proxies into the July 20 close.
XLE captures equity leverage to the same oil spike and geopolitical premium while diversifying pure futures-curve risk in USO.
PDBC provides diversified commodity beta that benefits if energy disruption broadens inflation and commodity risk premia this week.
JPM and WFC report July 14; higher 10y yields and solid bank positioning offer a catalyst path independent of pure energy beta.

portfolio_rationale: The dominant one-week catalyst is unresolved Strait of Hormuz control and the announced US blockade restart, which already lifted Brent sharply and can keep energy prices elevated through July 20. Concentrating in OIL, ENERGY, and BROAD_COMMODITIES targets that premium while a modest FINANCIALS sleeve adds bank-earnings upside without diluting the energy thesis.
rationale_summary: Allocate heavily to oil and energy equities for Hormuz/blockade risk premium, add broad commodities for spillover, and keep a smaller financials sleeve for July 14 bank results and higher yields.
